primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Inherited defects in motile-cilia structure, function, or biogenesis impair mucociliary clearance. Many affected individuals have dynein-arm or other axonemal defects, causing chronic sinopulmonary disease; abnormal embryonic nodal cilia can randomize left-right patterning, and flagellar dysfunction can impair fertility.
vignette: An 8-year-old boy has had year-round nasal congestion, recurrent otitis media, and a daily wet cough since infancy. Chest CT shows bronchiectasis. Cardiac examination reveals dextrocardia, and abdominal imaging shows mirror-image arrangement of the abdominal organs. Nasal nitric oxide is very low.
lead: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
distractor_notes: Cystic fibrosis can cause chronic sinopulmonary disease and bronchiectasis, but situs inversus with lifelong upper-airway disease and very low nasal nitric oxide strongly supports PCD.
Common variable immunodeficiency causes recurrent infections from impaired antibody production but does not characteristically cause situs inversus from motile-cilia dysfunction.
Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency primarily predisposes to emphysema and liver disease rather than childhood chronic otosinopulmonary disease with situs abnormalities.
Allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis occurs in susceptible patients with asthma or cystic fibrosis and does not explain congenital laterality abnormalities.
key_expl: Primary ciliary dyskinesia causes defective motile-cilia function with impaired mucociliary clearance, leading to chronic nasal, middle-ear, and lower-respiratory disease and bronchiectasis. Situs inversus occurs in a large subset because embryonic nodal cilia are required for normal left-right patterning. Very low nasal nitric oxide is a characteristic diagnostic clue.
objective: Recognize primary ciliary dyskinesia from chronic childhood otosinopulmonary disease, bronchiectasis, very low nasal nitric oxide, and situs inversus.
